item.title: Connectivity keeping pendant extensions of paths in $k$-connected triangle-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by Mader's conjecture on connectivity keeping trees, we study the corresponding problem in triangle-free graphs. For positive integers $k,m$, we first prove that every $k$-connected triangle-free graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\geq k+\left \lceil \frac{m}{2} \right \rceil $ contains a path $P$ of order $m$ such that $G-V(P)$ remains $k$-connected. Moreover, if $\kappa(G)=k$, then for every end $F$ of $G$ and every vertex $v\in F$, the path $P$ can be chosen in $G[F]$ with $v$ as an endvertex. If $\kappa(G)\geq k+1$, then any vertex of $G$ can be chosen as an endvertex of $P$. This result confirms the conjecture of Luo, Tian and Wu on connectivity keeping trees in bipartite graphs for all paths, and it also sharpens Fujita's path theorem to the optimal minimum degree bound. For an integer $i$ with $1\leq i\leq m-1$, let $P_m^+(i)$ denote the tree obtained from a path of order $m-1$ by adding one pendant vertex adjacent to its $i$th vertex. Let $(X,Y)$ be the bipartition of $P_m^+(i)$. We further prove that every $k$-connected triangle-free graph $G$ with $\delta(G)\geq k+\max\{|X|,|Y|\}$ contains a subgraph $T\cong P_m^+(i)$ such that $G-V(T)$ remains $k$-connected. The minimum degree bound is sharp, and the result confirms the bipartite conjecture for all pendant extensions of paths.
item.dc:creator: Menghan Ma, Qinghai Liu, Liping Zhang, Yanmei Hong

item.title: Cop number of $P_k$-free graphs without a claw or a fork
item.description: arXiv:2610.20129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2019, Liu proved that the cop number of any $(P_k, claw)$-free graph is at most $k-3$. In 2026, Clow and Meger improved and generalized the result of Liu by showing that every connected $(P_k, E)$-free graph has cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-1}{2} \rceil + 3$, where the graph $E$ is obtained by subdividing two edges of a claw. In this paper, we show that every $(P_k, claw)$-free graph $G$ has cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-1}{2} \rceil$. This improves the result of Clow and Meger on claw-free graphs. We further show that this bound can be improved to $\lceil \frac{k}{3}\rceil$, when $G$ contains a hole of length at least $k-1$. We show that the cop number of any $(P_k, fork)$-free graph is at most $\lceil \frac{2(k-1)}{3} \rceil$. This also improves the result of Clow and Meger on fork-free graphs for some values of $k$. We further show that every $(P_7, fork)$-free graph has cop number at most $3$, and this bound is tight.
item.dc:creator: Uttam K. Gupta, Dinabandhu Pradhan, Rashmi Rekha Swain

item.title: Elementary Proofs of Commonality of the House Graph and $K_4$ with One Edge Subdivided
item.description: arXiv:2610.20149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-coloring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random coloring with an equal proportion of each color. The house graph and $K_4$ with one edge subdivided once are known to be common by the flag algebra method. Grzesik, Lee, Lidick\'y, and Volec asked for ``human-friendly'' proofs of the commonality of these two graphs. In this short note, we give flag-algebra-free proofs that both graphs are common.
item.dc:creator: Hao Chen

item.title: The parity module of a matroid
item.description: arXiv:2610.20234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the parity module of a matroid with coefficients in a field $\mathbb{k}$. When $\mathbb{k}$ has characteristic zero, we show that the parity module of a matroid is isomorphic to its intersection cohomology module, yielding a new intrinsic characterization of the latter. The structure and dimension of the parity module can vary depending on the characteristic, giving rise to characteristic-dependent generalizations of the Kazhdan-Lusztig and Z-polynomials of matroids. When the matroid is realizable over the complex numbers, the parity module is isomorphic to the hypercohomology of the parity sheaf supported on the arrangement Schubert variety of any such realization. We also introduce the notion of pure modules over any field $\mathbb{k}$ and show that they satisfy a matroid analogue of the Beilinson-Bernstein-Deligne-Gabber decomposition theorem: Every pure module over the graded M\"obius algebra decomposes as a direct sum of shifts of the parity modules of matroids obtained by restricting to flats.
item.dc:creator: Tom Braden, June Huh, Jacob P. Matherne, Nicholas Proudfoot, Botong Wang

item.title: Nonexistence of Strongly Regular Graphs via Gegenbauer Positivity and SRG Counting
item.description: arXiv:2610.20259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a natural extension of the multipoint spherical semidefinite method of Liao and Yu~\cite{LY}, studying the interaction between semidefinite programming and strongly regular graph counting. Starting from the positive semidefinite kernels furnished by Gegenbauer polynomials, we express weighted kernel sums and counting identities in the same labelled induced-subgraph counts. Eliminating the counting equations gives a semidefinite feasibility problem. Numerical dual solutions guide the construction of rational certificates, whose contradiction identities are verified exactly. Our aim is a systematic method that treats many parameter sets through the same construction. For least eigenvalue $-3$, it gives new counting certificates for $(351,140,73,44)$, $(550,162,75,36)$, $(703,182,81,35)$ and $(1344,221,88,26)$, previously excluded by Liao and Yu~\cite[Theorem~1]{LY}, and for six additional parameter sets: \[ \begin{array}{@{}lll@{}} (375,102,45,21), & (405,132,63,33), & (441,88,35,13),\\ (476,133,60,28), & (540,147,66,30), & (575,112,45,16). \end{array} \] Seven certificates use Gegenbauer positivity and counting information alone at the displayed orders. The cases $v=375,441,575$ additionally use proved short-vector restrictions, unique vertex extensions, and integer common-neighbour inequalities. The proofs end in displayed inequalities with incompatible signs. Their justification is given by the dual identities and the proved positivity and counting relations; accompanying code automates the longer rational arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Zhen-Qi Liao, Jiaxin Wang, Wei-Hsuan Yu, Jianfeng Cai

item.title: A new generalization of parking functions: $\rho$-Naples parking functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new model of parking functions, called $\rho$-Naples parking functions, in which each car has a certain number of spots to check preceding its preferred one before looking for available spots by moving forward. This notion, where each car has its own number of previous spots to check, generalizes that of Naples parking function, where this number is the same for all cars. We start by showing that, for a given sequence of preferences for each car, a successful parking strategy (that is, an assignment of how many backward spots each car is allowed to check) remains successful if we increase the number of backwards spots to check for some of the cars. This means that the set of successful strategies for a given parking preference is an up-set in the lattice of parking strategies, which raises the intriguing question of characterizing such up-sets. Though we are not able to completely solve this problem, we provide a characterization of those successful strategies which minimize the total number of allowed backward steps for a given parking preference, and we determine a lower bound for the number of cars which are allowed to move backwards (also showing that it can be attained). To conclude, we analyze the specific situation in which each car can take at most one backward step, and we completely characterize the set of successful parking preferences in this case.
item.dc:creator: Luca Ferrari, Francesco Verciani

item.title: Power quotients of plactic-like monoids
item.description: arXiv:2610.20317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we describe the quotients of several plactic-like monoids by the least congruences containing the relations $a^{\sigma(a)} = a$ for $\sigma(a) \geq 2$ for every generator $a$. The starting point of this paper is the recent paper of Reutenauer and the first author about the stylic monoid. This monoid is the quotient of the plactic monoid by the relations $a^2 = a$ for every generator $a$. The plactic-like monoids considered here are the plactic monoid itself, the Chinese monoid, the hypoplactic monoid, the sylvester monoid, the metasylvester and hyposylvester monoids. In each case we describe a set of normal forms and the idempotents. We obtain formulae for their cardinalities and we describe their isomorphism types.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Abram, Florent Hivert, James D. Mitchell, Jean-Christophe Novelli, Maria Tsalakou

item.title: A Unified Linear Programming Approach for Maximizing Vertex-Degree-Based Indices of Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.20364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The problem of maximizing vertex-degree-based topological indices over trees with a prescribed order and maximum degree $\Delta$ has traditionally relied on ad-hoc combinatorial arguments. In this paper, we establish a unified linear programming approach that systematically resolves these extremal problems. By formulating the optimization over degree-pair multiplicities, the search for an extremal tree reduces to minimizing a discrete dual penalty. Treating vertex degrees as continuous variables yields an analytical single-variable test condition that guarantees global optimality. We apply this framework across a diverse collection of invariants. We prove that the standard basic feasible solution is optimal for the Tangent Sombor, $SO_1$, $SO_2$, Albertson, and $\sigma$-irregularity indices for all $\Delta \ge 3$. However, the dual optimality conditions establish exact analytical thresholds at which the standard basis loses optimality, necessitating a transition to alternative basic feasible solutions. For the Arithmetic-Geometric ($AG$) index, the standard basis is optimal strictly for $\Delta \ge 9$; for smaller maximum degrees ($3 \le \Delta \le 8$), optimization shifts to an alternative edge basis, allowing us to explicitly construct and characterize all extremal trees across congruence classes, including chemical trees ($\Delta \in \{3, 4\}$). Conversely, for the Triangle Volume index ($SO_{11}$), the standard basis is optimal exclusively for $\Delta \le 8$, while for $\Delta \ge 9$ we analytically derive a novel, degree-dependent optimal basis to explicitly construct its extremal configurations.
item.dc:creator: Milan Ba\v{s}i\'{c}

item.title: Potatoes and Onions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The first major step in the theory of graph minors of Robertson and Seymour was the grid theorem, a fundamental duality result describing that any graph of sufficiently high treewidth must contain a large grid as a minor. Since this pioneering work, multiple grid theorems have been established in structural graph theory, linking various width parameters of combinatorial objects with the non-existence of grid-like obstructions. In particular, Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC'15] proved a variant of the grid theorem for directed graphs that links directed treewidth with the non-existence of topological minors of large cylindrical walls. On the other hand, to study immersions of undirected graphs $-$ another containment relation that focuses on edge-disjointness, rather than vertex-disjointness $-$ Wollan [JCTB'15] introduced a parameter, tree-cutwidth, and proved that it is dual to immersions of large walls. In this work, we present a version of Wollan's parameter for directed graphs, the directed tree-cutwidth. The main result is a grid theorem for directed tree-cutwidth, establishing that it is dual to directed immersions of large cylindrical walls.
item.dc:creator: Marcin Bria\'nski, Meike Hatzel, Karolina Okrasa, Micha{\l} Pilipczuk

item.title: Treewidth and the Product of Tree-Independence and Tree-Chromatic Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.20407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$, let $\mathrm{tw}(G)$, $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\alpha(G)$, and $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\chi(G)$ denote its treewidth, tree-independence number, and tree-chromatic number, respectively. We prove that every nonempty graph $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{tw}(G)+1\leq\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\alpha(G)\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\chi(G)(1+\lfloor\log_2(\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\alpha(G))\rfloor)$. This improves the quadratic bound of Koutsoutis, Krause, Liu, Redzic, and Ueckerdt. For every pair of integers $n,k\geq2$, we construct a graph $G$ with $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\alpha(G)=n$, $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}\chi(G)=k$, and $\mathrm{tw}(G)=\Omega(nk\log_2 n)$. Thus the upper bound is best possible up to a constant factor.
item.dc:creator: Xinheng Lin

item.title: Two Perfect One-Factorizations of $K_{92}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A perfect 1-factorization of the complete graph $K_{2t}$ is a partition of its edges into perfect matchings such that the union of any two of them is a Hamilton cycle. Kotzig conjectured in 1963 that $K_{2t}$ has a perfect 1-factorization for every $t \ge 2$, but apart from some infinite families and a list of sporadic orders the conjecture is open, and $92$ was one of the nine orders up to $100$ for which no perfect 1-factorization was known. In this paper we construct two non-isomorphic perfect 1-factorizations of $K_{92}$.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Maciosowski

item.title: The terminal leave in random greedy hypergraph matching
item.description: arXiv:2610.20414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be the terminal graph of the random triangle-removal process started from $K_n$. We prove that $e(G)/n^{3/2}\to1/(2\sqrt2)$ in $L^2$. More generally, we obtain the analogous result for any fixed strictly $k$-balanced $k$-graph. Our main tool is a more general theorem on random greedy matchings in nearly regular uniform hypergraphs with few short cycles under a stability assumption on the survival equations.
item.dc:creator: Peter Keevash

item.title: Intersecting families of loose spanning hypertrees
item.description: arXiv:2610.20443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A loose hypertree is a hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree. Let $b\ge3$, $n\equiv1\pmod{b-1}$, and $s:=(n-1)/(b-1)$. We determine the largest $t$-intersecting families of loose spanning $b$-uniform hypertrees on $[n]$, simultaneously for every $1\le t\le s$, provided $n$ exceeds an explicit constant depending only on $b$. The extremal families consist of all such hypertrees containing a fixed $t$-edge loose forest whose component sizes are as equal as the divisibility condition permits. In particular, when $bt\le n$, the extremal forests are matchings. We also prove a Hilton--Milner-type bound: if $n\ge C_b(t+1)$, where $C_b$ depends only on $b$, every nontrivial $t$-intersecting family has at most $(s+1)r_{t+1}(n)$ members. Here $r_j(n)$ is the maximum possible number of loose spanning $b$-uniform hypertrees containing a fixed $j$-edge loose forest. For fixed constants $b,t$, this bound is asymptotically sharp and is $O_{b,t}(n^{2-b})r_t(n)$. The proofs combine exact forest enumeration with the intersection theorems of Kupavskii for spread families.
item.dc:creator: Yury Person, Thomas Schweser

item.title: The $k$-color poset Ramsey number of the diamond is $2k$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $k$-color Ramsey number of a poset $P$ is the smallest dimension $d$ such that any $k$-coloring of the $d$-dimensional Boolean lattice contains a monochromatic induced copy of $P$. For $ j\ge 2$ the $j$-diamond is the poset that consists of a maximum element, a minimum element and an antichain of size $j$. We prove that the $k$-color Ramsey number of the $j$-diamond is at most $jk$. Colorings of the Boolean lattice that assign sets of the same size the same color provide matching lower bounds for $j \in \{2,3,4\}$.
item.dc:creator: Tom Bohman, Will Cong, Quentin Dubroff, Teresa Huang, Zheyuan Li, BangTam Ngo

item.title: Hypergraphs with the smallest Hall ratio are still hard to colour
item.description: arXiv:2610.20562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $H$ a hypergraph, the Hall ratio $\rho(H)=\text{max}_{X\subseteq V(H)}\frac{\lvert{X}\rvert}{\alpha(H[X])}$ is a natural lower bound for its chromatic number, and among non-empty $k$-uniform hypergraphs the smallest possible Hall ratio is $k/(k-1)$. For graphs ($k = 2$), having minimum Hall ratio $2$ forces chromatic number $2$. Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il, R\"{o}dl, and Sales asked whether a similar phenomenon holds at higher uniformities. We answer this question negatively in a strong form, showing that for every $k \geqslant 3$ there are $k$-uniform hypergraphs with Hall ratio exactly $k/(k-1)$ and arbitrarily large fractional chromatic number.
item.dc:creator: Veronica Bitonti, Freddie Illingworth, Pedram Noohi, Jane Tan

item.title: Decay-Ramsey Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.20577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a sequence $\mathbf{a}=(a_i)_{i\geq 1}$ of positive real numbers, we say that a colouring $c:E(K_n)\to \mathbb{N}$ is $\mathbf{a}$-bounded if the proportion of edges coloured $i$ is at most $a_i$, for all $i$. We write \[ \mathbf{a}\, \to\, K_k \] if, for all sufficiently large $n$, all $\mathbf{a}$-bounded colourings $c:E(K_n)\to \mathbb{N}$ contain a monochromatic $K_k$. We say that the sequence $\mathbf{a}$ is \emph{Decay-Ramsey} if $\mathbf{a}\to K_k$ for all $k\ge 2$. In this short paper we introduce the question of determining which sequences are Decay-Ramsey and present some initial results.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Di Braccio, Simon Griffiths, Pedram Noohi, Leo Versteegen

item.title: The Online Steinitz Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16715v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by Steinitz's celebrated result (1913) and recent online vector-balancing results of Kulkarni et al. (2024) and Aden-Ali (2026), we introduce the online Steinitz problem: $T$ vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, each of $\ell_2$-norm at most $1$ and with total sum zero, arrive one at a time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably to unused positions of an array. The goal is to keep every prefix sum of the resulting order small. We first obtain deterministic prefix-discrepancy bounds of $O(\log T)$ for $d=1$ and $O(\sqrt T)$ for $d\ge2$. Our main contribution is a general reduction that converts deterministic and randomized online vector-balancing algorithms, which assign signs to arriving vectors, into online ordering algorithms. Combined with recent vector-balancing results, this yields a randomized algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log T+\sqrt{d\log T})$ and running time $O(dT\log T)$. The guarantee holds with high probability against an oblivious adversary. The reduction also gives bounds for sparse vectors and extends to inputs in arbitrary compact convex bodies. Finally, we prove matching lower bounds in both the deterministic and randomized cases.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Russo, Jiaye Wei

item.title: Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones: a five-party gap and dependence on the local dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.18905v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy linear inequalities; for stabilizer states, the backbone of quantum error correction, the achievable entropy vectors generate a convex cone. We show that, after a linear lift, the closure of this cone is exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object on one more element than there are parties: the closed cone generated by the rank functions of arrangements of subspaces over $\mathrm{GF}(d)$ for a prime local dimension $d$, and of subgroups of abelian groups of exponent dividing $d$ in general. This correspondence brings two features of rank inequalities into play. First, the purifier acts as an extra variable: already for five parties the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, with which earlier evidence suggested it might coincide; an explicit six-variable inequality witnesses the gap. Second, the characteristic of the field enters, so the cone depends on the local dimension. It does not for up to four parties. With enough parties, the cone of $\mathbb{Z}_d$ qudits is contained in that of $\mathbb{Z}_{d'}$ qudits if and only if $d$ divides $d'$, and already for six parties the logical zero state of Steane's code lies outside the stabilizer cone of every odd local dimension. For this last result we show that the seven-variable characteristic-dependent inequalities we checked all follow from Shannon inequalities on the self-dual slice, and instead transfer one of them through a family of subgroups derived from the Fano plane.
item.dc:creator: Xidan Song, Ruifeng Cao

item.title: Short Proofs for the Minimum Number of Determined Circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.18918v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present short proofs for the main parts of the recently completed solution of Erd\H{o}s Problem 506, which asks for the minimum number of distinct circles determined by a finite planar point set that is neither collinear nor concyclic. An inversion argument and a seven-point line lemma show that eight points determine at least $17$ circles, and an explicit configuration attains this bound. A single argument combining Melchior's inequality with Langer's incidence bound establishes the sharp formula for every $n\ge15$. The proofs give concise alternatives to longer arguments in the recent literature; the remaining finite cases are cited separately.
item.dc:creator: Stijn Cambie, Denis Paliy, Rafa{\l} Wrona

item.title: A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.19193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an infinite family of solutions to the Mondrian art problem with absolute defect bounded above by $280$, of side lengths $n_0 = 315$, $n_1 = 106785$, and $n_{j+2} = 340n_{j+1} - n_j$, where $n_j$ is congruent to $315 \pmod{630}$. This absolute bound shows that the minimum defect does not necessarily increase with $n$, providing a counterexample to a conjecture which has been open since the problem's original proposal. Our design is derived from a well-known seven-rectangle dissection over the real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{19})$, with non-integer side lengths; we tailor the side lengths to be integers via an infinite Pell family. Using the same method, we devise a second family with defect $560$ that contains infinitely many side lengths which are divisible by any given positive integer, implying that for any $k$ there are infinitely many side lengths $n \equiv 0 \pmod{k}$ with defect bounded above by $560$. This constant bound offers a dramatic improvement on the previous quadratic bounds.
item.dc:creator: Cooper O'Kuhn, Freeman Slaughter

item.title: Orthogonal partition by four hyperplanes
item.description: arXiv:2610.19214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study orthogonal $(4,3)$-equipartitions of finite measures absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure: every three of four mutually orthogonal affine hyperplanes must divide each measure into eight equal parts. For every number $m$ of measures, we determine the exact dimension threshold of Musin's polynomial criterion and express it in terms of the binary expansion of $m$. The threshold coincides with the geometric lower bound precisely when $m=2^j-1$. Consequently, $\Delta^*(2^j-1,4,3)=7\cdot2^{j-1}-2$ for every $j\geq1$.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Fakhrutdinov, Platon Khamatov, Oleg R. Musin

item.title: An oral history of FPSAC
item.description: arXiv:2610.19236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As its 40th anniversary nears, we present a history of the International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics (FPSAC), through interviews with figures from its past, present, and future.
item.dc:creator: Sam Hopkins

item.title: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
item.description: arXiv:2610.19434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $\rho\colon G\to \GSp_{2n}(\Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ associated with $\rho$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $\rho$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by $\rho$. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\GSp_{2n}(\Q_p)$, under some assumptions, we prove the existence of certain paths in $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ and show that $\Gamma_\rho^\GSp$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Aniruddha Sudarshan

item.title: The Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-Complete
item.description: arXiv:2610.19558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Poset games form a fundamental class of combinatorial games that includes classical games such as Nim and Chomp. Determining the outcome of a poset game is known to be PSPACE-complete even for posets of height at most three. However, the exact computational complexity of Two-Level Poset Game, played on posets of height at most two, has remained an open problem for over a decade. We resolve this problem by proving that Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-complete via a polynomial-time reduction from Avoid True on positive CNF formulas.
item.dc:creator: Kengo Hashimoto

item.title: Maximum Likelihood Degrees via One-Edge Chordal Completion
item.description: arXiv:2610.19669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The maximum likelihood degree of a Gaussian graphical model measures the algebraic complexity of its likelihood equations. This paper studies maximum likelihood degrees of Gaussian graphical models through chordal completion. When a graph becomes chordal after one missing edge is added, its maximum likelihood degree is determined by the maximal cliques and clique-tree separators containing that edge. This recovers Uhler's formula for complete bipartite graphs with one part of size two, and extends it to deleted-spine clique books, whose degree is unchanged when a page is thickened to a clique. For several fill edges, the same method gives a product formula when no clique or separator bag contains two fill edges. We also determine four classes of vertices at which clique blow-up preserves the degree. Two follow from known results, and two are established here.
item.dc:creator: Nilava Metya

item.title: Nonlinear fixed-distance codes via real lifts of moment configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19960v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A_q(n,d)$ denote the largest size of a code of length $n$ and minimum Hamming distance $d$ over an alphabet of $q$ symbols. For fixed $q\ge2$ and $d\ge4$ we construct codes with redundancy $n-\log_q A_q(n,d)\le(d-3)\log_q n+O(\sqrt{\log n})$ for all large $n$. No algebraic structure is imposed on the alphabet, and the codes are not linear. For $d=4$ and $d=5$ the coefficient of $\log_q n$ matches the Hamming bound, so the redundancy is determined up to lower-order terms. At distance four the codes are provably better than every linear code: by the polynomial-method bound for cap sets, $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes with $q>2$ require a strictly larger coefficient in front of $\log_q n$. The construction imposes moment checksums over an auxiliary finite field, as BCH codes do, but one fewer than the distance would normally require. The affine-line theorem from prior work describes the dependencies left by these checks. We exclude them by placing the code positions inside a specially structured subset of the field, built from Behrend's sphere construction with the help of algebraic number theory.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Yekhanin

item.title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
item.description: arXiv:2610.19980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extremal constructions play a central role in the design and analysis of algorithms. Integrality-gap instances expose the limitations of relaxations, while hard configurations reveal structural sources of computational difficulty. Such constructions, however, are still typically discovered through a slow, manual process. This paper investigates how machine learning can accelerate their discovery to support algorithm design and analysis. We build on PatternBoost, a framework alternating local search with generation from a trained transformer, using its Axplorer implementation to investigate three problems: integrality gaps for maximum independent set of rectangles, integrality gaps for stabbing unit squares with axis-parallel lines, and hard instances for recursive guillotine cutting. By exploring candidate representations, local search operations, and surrogate models used to rank candidates before exact verification, we carefully adapt the framework to these combinatorial geometry problems.While naive representations and search strategies fail to find non-trivial instances, our tailored adaptation discovers numerous non-trivial constructions. For stabbing unit squares, the method reaches a gap of $20/13\approx 1.54$, improving on the literature's best known lower bound of $3/2$. Purely automated search converges rapidly and then plateaus, prompting the question of what is required to push the bound higher still. We find that initial instance diversity plays an important role: with modest expert input via a structured staircase construction, the system reaches an improved integrality gap of $14/9\approx 1.555$. These results demonstrate that machine learning and domain expertise can be combined to discover new extremal constructions that advance algorithmic lower bounds.
item.dc:creator: Deepak Ajwani, Paula Carroll, Rishikesh Gajjala, Ananta Manoranjan, Ryan O'Connor, Rajiv Raman, Saurabh Ray, Aimen Taha

item.title: Quantized six-vertex realizations of frustration graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A recent graph-theoretic criterion for a Hamiltonian to exhibit a free-parafermion spectrum is that its frustration graph be an indifference graph. We show that an arbitrary finite indifference graph can be realized as a frustration graph of the quantized six-vertex model at odd roots of unity, by a suitable choice of the defining wiring diagram and parameters. This provides a concrete realization of the criterion through the quantum Frobenius property of the quantized six-vertex model, recently established from its three-dimensional integrable structure.
item.dc:creator: Atsuo Kuniba, Souta Oikawa

item.title: Quantitative lower bound for Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers
item.description: arXiv:2610.20311v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each positive integer $N$, let $p_i$ be the $i$-th prime for $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and set $$ \Phi_N=\left\{\prod_{i=1}^{N}p_i^{a_i}:a_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}\right\}. $$ Write $f(N)$ for the largest cardinality of a subset of $\Phi_N$ containing no two distinct legs of an integral right triangle. We prove $$ N^{N-1}(\log\log\log N)\ll f(N). $$
item.dc:creator: Rongzhong Xiao

item.title: Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2610.20368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.
item.dc:creator: Sanjaye Ramgoolam, Micha{\l} Studzi\'nski

item.title: Topological recursion for spin enumeration of hypermaps
item.description: arXiv:2610.20464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish topological recursion for the spin enumeration of hypermaps, or, in the dual language, spin dessins d'enfants. This problem has remarkable features distinguishing it from other applications of topological recursion to enumerative combinatorics. First, the spectral curve is elliptic rather than rational, as in most cases studied before. Second, it contains degenerate ramification points, and one has to apply a version of degenerate topological recursion. Finally, the meromorphic correlator differentials have "moving" poles on the antidiagonals between pairs of distinct arguments, and one has to adjust the loop equations to this kind of degeneracy as well. The computations involve concepts of different kinds, such as BKP integrability, Gaussian integrals, the x-y swap, and symplectic duality.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Alexandrov, Boris Bychkov, Petr Dunin-Barkowski, Maxim Kazarian, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: Claw-Free and Line Graph Edge Deletion on Block Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Edge deletion problems ask for the fewest edges whose deletion gives a graph with a specified property. We study two such problems on block graphs. First making the graph claw-free, and second making it a line graph. Since every line graph is claw-free, the second problem is at least as difficult as the first. We show that on block graphs the two optimum values are always equal, and both are attained by the line graph of a forest. The main step is a completion argument, in which starting from any claw-free solution, we put back edges to get some nice structure inside each block still maintaining the claw-free property. This reduces both edge-deletion problems to the same problem of selecting vertices within the blocks of the input graph. We solve it by dynamic programming in $O(n+m)$ time, which also produces an optimal deletion set and a forest whose line graph is what remains after the completion argument. We also extend the method to $K_{1,r+1}$-free edge deletion for every fixed $r$.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Adak

item.title: Minimal Resolutions of $k$-divisible and $(k-1)$-dominant Ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.20565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce invariants we call $k$-divisibility and $d$-dominance, which are combinatorial constraints on the minimal generators of monomial ideals. We then prove that $k$ (respectively, $d$) is an upper bound (respectively, lower bound) for the projective dimension of a $k$-divisible (respectively, $d$-dominant) monomial ideal. This leads us to an explicit minimal resolution of $k$-divisible, $d$-dominant ideals when $d=k-1$ via a Lyubeznik resolution. This framework allows us to prove a conjecture made by Alesandroni. Using these invariants, we also provide a characterization of monomial ideals whose minimal free resolution is attainable from the Taylor resolution by performing exactly one consecutive cancellation. We also prove that for all $q,k,d$ in the range $1\leq d<k \leq q-1$, there exist monomial ideals that are $k$-divisible and $d$-dominant with $q$ minimal generators.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Welte, Guillermo Alesandroni

item.title: Sparse universal graphs for planarity
item.description: arXiv:2010.05779v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that for every integer $n\geq 1$ there exists a graph $G_n$ with $(1+o(1))n$ vertices and $n^{1 + o(1)}$ edges such that every $n$-vertex planar graph is isomorphic to a subgraph of $G_n$. The best previous bound on the number of edges was $O(n^{3/2})$, proved by Babai, Chung, Erd\H{o}s, Graham, and Spencer in 1982. We then show that for every integer $n\geq 1$ there is a graph $U_n$ with $n^{1 + o(1)}$ vertices and edges that contains induced copies of every $n$-vertex planar graph. This significantly reduces the number of edges in a recent construction of the authors with Dujmovi\'c, Gavoille, and Micek.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of the London Mathematical Society, 108/4:1333--1357, 2023
item.dc:creator: Louis Esperet, Gwena\"el Joret, Pat Morin

item.title: On composition and decomposition operations for vector spaces, graphs and matroids
item.description: arXiv:2305.16354v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the ideas of composition and decomposition in the context of vector spaces, graphs and matroids. For vector spaces $\V_{AB},$ treated as collection of row vectors, with specified column set $A\uplus B,$ we define $\V_{SP}\lrarv \V_{PQ}, S\cap Q= \emptyset, $ to be the collection of all vectors $(f_S,f_Q)$ such that $(f_S,f_P)\in \V_{SP}, (f_P,f_Q)\in \V_{PQ}$. An analogous operation $\G_{SP}\lrarg \G_{PQ}\equivd \G_{PQ}$ can be defined in relation to graphs $\G_{SP}, \G_{PQ},$ on edge sets $S\uplus P, P\uplus Q,$ respectively in terms of an overlapping subgraph $\G_P$ which gets deleted in the right side graph (see for instance the notion of $k-sum$ \cite{oxley}). For matroids we define the `linking' $\M_{SP}\lrarm \M_{PQ} \equivd (\M_{SP}\vee \M_{PQ})\times (S\uplus Q)$, denoting the contraction operation by '$\times$'. In each case, we examine how to minimize the size of the `overlap' set $P,$ without affecting the right side entity. In the case of vector spaces, there is a polynomial time algorithm for achieving the minimum, which we present. Similar ideas work for graphs and for matroids under appropriate conditions. Next we consider the problem of decomposition. Here, in the case of vector spaces, the problem is to decompose $\V_{SQ}$ as $\V_{SP}\lrarv \V_{PQ},$ with minimum size $P.$ We give a polynomial time algorithm for this purpose. In the case of graphs and matroids we give a solution to this problem under certain restrictions.
item.dc:creator: H. Narayanan

item.title: Best possible upper bounds on the restrained domination number of cubic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2403.17129v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A dominating set in a graph $G$ is a set $S$ of vertices such that every vertex in $V(G) \setminus S$ is adjacent to a vertex in $S$. A restrained dominating set of $G$ is a dominating set $S$ with the additional restraint that the graph $G - S$ obtained by removing all vertices in $S$ is isolate-free. The domination number $\gamma(G)$ and the restrained domination number $\gamma_{r}(G)$ are the minimum cardinalities of a dominating set and restrained dominating set, respectively, of $G$. Let $G$ be a cubic graph of order~$n$. A classical result of Reed [Combin. Probab. Comput. 5 (1996), 277--295] states that $\gamma(G) \le \frac{3}{8}n$, and this bound is best possible. To determine a best possible upper bound on the restrained domination number of $G$ is more challenging, and we prove that $\gamma_{r}(G) \le \frac{2}{5}n$.
item.dc:creator: Bo\v{s}tjan Bre\v{s}ar, Michael A. Henning

item.title: Exploring the unleaved tree of numerical semigroups up to a given genus
item.description: arXiv:2503.14664v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a new algorithm for exploring or counting the numerical semigroups of a given genus that uses the unleaved version of the tree of numerical semigroups. In the unleaved tree there are no leaves rather than the ones at depth equal to the genus in consideration. For exploring the unleaved tree we present a new encoding system of a numerical semigroup given by the gcd of its left elements and its shrinking, that is, the semigroup generated by its left elements divided by their gcd. We show a method to determine the right generators and strong generators of a semigroup by means of the gcd and the shrinking encoding, as well as a method to encode a semigroup from the encoding of its parent or of its preceding sibling. With the new algorithm, we obtained $n_{76}=29028294421710227$ and $n_{77}=47008818196495180$.
item.dc:creator: Maria Bras-Amor\'os

item.title: On a question about real rooted polynomials and f-polynomials of simplicial complexes
item.description: arXiv:2503.24076v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a polynomial $f(t) = 1+f_0t+\cdots +f_{d-1}t^d$ with positive integer coefficients Bell and Skandera ask if real rootedness of f(t) implies that there is a simplicial complex with f-vector $(1,f_0 \ldots,f_{d-1})$. In this paper we discover properties implied by the real rootedness of f(t) in terms of the binomial representation $f_i = \binom{x_{i+1}}{i+1}, i \geq 0$. We use these to provide a sufficient criterion for a positive answer to the question by Bell and Skandera. We also describe two further approaches to the conjecture and use one to verify that some well studied real rooted classical polynomials are f-polynomials. Finally, we provide a series of results showing that the set of f-vectors of simplicial complexes is closed under constructions also preserving real rootedness of their generating polynomials.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Adv. in Appl. Math. 175 (2026), Paper No. 103041, 16 pp
item.dc:creator: Lili Mu, Volkmar Welker

item.title: Permutations with a fixed number of occurrences of a monotone pattern
item.description: arXiv:2506.05712v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We bound the number of permutations with a fixed number $r$ of $321 \ominus p_0$ patterns by a constant times the number of permutations which avoid $321 \ominus p_0$. We use this new upper bound to show that the ordinary generating function for permutations with $r$ copies of $k(k-1)...1$ is not rational for odd $k \geq 3$ and not algebraic for even $k \geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Waite

item.title: $2$-large sets are sets of Bohr recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2512.01997v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d$ be real numbers, fix $\delta>0$, and let $S$ be the set of positive integers $s$ such that $\|\alpha_i s\|_{\R/\Z}>\delta$ for some $1\le i\le d$. We prove that $S$ is not \enquote{$2$-large}, i.e. there is a $2$-coloring of $\N$ that avoids arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common differences in $S$. The case $d=1$ was previously known; here we prove the result in every finite dimension.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss

item.title: Classifying integer tilings and hypertilings
item.description: arXiv:2601.21445v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: There are two objectives to this work: to classify all tame integer tilings and to classify all tame integer hypertilings. Motivation for the first objective comes from Conway and Coxeter's modelling of positive integer friezes using triangulated polygons, which has received significant attention since the discovery of cluster algebras by Fomin and Zelevinsky in 2002. Assem, Reutenauer, and Smith introduced $\text{SL}_2$-tilings as generalisations of friezes, and Bessenrodt, Holm, and J{\o}rgensen classified positive integer $\text{SL}_2$-tilings using infinite triangulated polygons. Here we consider $N$-tilings, of which $\text{SL}_2$-tilings are the case $N=1$. We provide a geometric model for all tame integer $N$-tilings using a generalisation of the Farey graph in the hyperbolic plane. Highlights of this model include classifications of all positive integer $N$-tilings and of all positive rational friezes, with entries encoded by lambda lengths or weight data of triangulated polygons. The second objective is motivated by Bhargava's celebrated study of binary quadratic forms using integer cubes and by an observation of Demonet et al. that there is essentially only one three-dimensional positive integer tiling with $\text{SL}_2$ cross sections. We consider a richer class of three-dimensional tilings, which we call hypertilings, using the Cayley hyperdeterminant. We classify all tame integer hypertilings using generalised Farey graphs; remarkably, those with Cayley hyperdeterminant 1 prove to have a simple description in terms of triple Hadamard products of integer pairs.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Karpenkov, Ian Short, Matty van Son, Andrei Zabolotskii

item.title: Multidimensional convolution matrices and perfect colorings of subspace hypergraphs applied for bent functions and related designs
item.description: arXiv:2602.14569v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The main aim of the present paper is to introduce new methods for the study of combinatorial designs related to bent functions. They are based on interpretations of convolution on finite abelian groups as multiplication by a multidimensional matrix and designs as perfect colorings of subspace hypergraphs of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. We establish a correspondence between eigenfunctions of convolution matrices and perfect colorings of subspace hypergraphs, show that perfect colorings of subspace hypergraphs admit a characterization in terms of convolution and that two-valued eigenfunctions of subspace hypergraphs correspond to perfect colorings. As applications, we represent partial difference sets, bent and plateaued Boolean functions, spreads, and strong bent partitions of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ as eigenfunctions of convolution matrices and as perfect colorings of subspace hypergraphs. We also find some eigenvalues of convolution matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and $\mathbb{F}_3^n$.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir N. Potapov, Anna A. Taranenko

item.title: Almost amorphic association schemes
item.description: arXiv:2604.06538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An association scheme is called amorphic if every possible fusion of relations gives rise to another association scheme. In earlier work, we showed that if an association scheme has at most one relation that is neither strongly regular of Latin square type nor strongly regular of negative Latin square type, then it must be amorphic. We now construct non-amorphic $d$-class association schemes in which precisely two relations are not strongly regular of Latin square type or strongly regular of negative Latin square type, for any $d \geq 4$. We also raise the question whether different types of strongly regular graphs can coexist in an association scheme. Among some other results, we show that if one of the relations is a lattice graph, then any other strongly regular relation in the scheme must be of Latin square type.
item.dc:creator: Edwin van Dam, Jack H. Koolen, Yanzhen Xiong

item.title: The Distribution of the Deepest Leaves in Binary Trees
item.description: arXiv:2605.12821v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the extreme local structure of plane binary trees through the limiting distribution of the number of leaves at maximum depth. For every $m\geq1$, we determine the limiting probability $\kappa^{[m]}$ that the deepest level contains $2m$ leaves. The resulting sequence is encoded by a generating function $K(y)$, obtained from a bivariate refinement of the Catalan iteration. We show that, at the critical point of this iteration, a parabolic recurrence governs the marked generating functions. Using continuous iteration theory and a Fatou coordinate, we transform this recurrence into the functional equation $K((1+y/4)^2)=K(y)+4$, which describes the limiting law. Its singular behavior yields the exponential tail $\kappa^{[m]}\sim4^{-m+1}$. Numerical evaluation gives, e.g., $\kappa^{[1]}\approx0.7009$, $\kappa^{[2]}\approx0.2226$ and an average number of deepest leaves equal to $\hat{\kappa}=4\kappa^{[1]}\approx2.8037$.
item.dc:creator: Olivier Bodini, Antoine Genitrini, Khaydar Nurligareev

item.title: Spanning-Tree Maximization Forces Isoperimetry in the Square Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2605.23773v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine which connected sets of $N$ vertices in the square lattice support the most spanning trees, using all lattice edges between the chosen vertices. Every maximizer minimizes the number of edges joining the set to the rest of the lattice. Its shape is a rectangle with at most two straight strips of vertices removed at opposite corners. For $N\ge18$, the maximizer is unique up to translation, rotation, and reflection: an explicitly determined rectangle with one possibly empty corner strip removed along its longer side. The proof combines comparisons of Laplacian determinants with geometric comparisons of corner deletions. For $N=n^2$, we prove a sharp stability inequality that bounds the symmetric difference from a translated $n\times n$ square in terms of the loss in logarithmic tree count. Thus, nearly optimal tree counts force the vertex set to be close to a square. We also derive an exact product formula and a recurrence for the number of spanning trees in rectangles with a single corner strip removed.
item.dc:creator: Jiechen Zhang

item.title: Biclique decompositions from Welzl orders
item.description: arXiv:2606.09785v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A biclique decomposition of a graph is a partition of its edges into complete bipartite subgraphs. We consider graphs whose vertices can be ordered such that the neighborhood of every vertex is the union of a sublinear number of intervals. We observe that these graphs admit compact representations in the form of biclique decompositions of small size. Here, the size of a decomposition is measured as the sum of the number of vertices of its bicliques. Combining this result with the existence of suitable vertex orderings for graphs of low neighborhood complexity, as proven by Welzl in 1988, we recover and extend several known results up to logarithmic factors. These results include upper bounds on the Zarankiewicz problem, matrix multiplication, quantum circuit complexity, and shortest path algorithms in "well-structured" instances.
item.dc:creator: Jean Cardinal, Rose McCarty, Yelena Yuditsky

item.title: Locating a Seymour vertex in oriented graphs having minimum outdegree at most 7
item.description: arXiv:2606.30588v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A vertex $v$ of an oriented graph $D$ is a Seymour vertex if the number of outneighbors of $v$ is less than or equal to the number of second outneighbors of $v$ (vertices at directed distance exactly $2$ from $v$). Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture claims that every oriented graph contains a Seymour vertex. We propose the following stronger conjecture (Conjecture 1.4): given any oriented graphs $D$, there exists a minimum outdegree vertex $s$, and a Seymour vertex $v^*$ such that the directed distance from $s$ to $v^*$ is at most $\lfloor\frac{\delta^+(D)}{3} \rfloor$, where $\delta^+(D)$ denotes the minimum outdegree of $D$. The main contribution of this article is to show that Conjecture 1.4 is true for all oriented graphs having minimum outdegree at most $7$. This, in particular, improves the results of Kaneko and Locke (2001) which (implicitly) proved Conjecture 1.4 for all oriented graphs having minimum outdegree at most $6$. In particular, this yields Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture for this class of oriented graphs. We also construct a family of digraphs attaining the proposed distance bound, showing that it cannot be improved in general. Finally, by adapting existing arguments, we show that if Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture is true then given any oriented graph $D$ and any vertex $v$, it is always possible to find a Seymour vertex $v^*$ such that the directed distance from $v$ to $v^*$ is at most the outdegree of $v$.
item.dc:creator: Arpan Sadhukhan, Sagnik Sen

item.title: Forbidding $r$-extension of $C_4$ -- a counterexample of the Anstee-Sali conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.07646v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note we prove $\mathrm{forb}(n,\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4)=\Theta(n^{r-1/2})$, thus providing a series of counterexamples of a 2005 conjecture of the first two authors. Here $\mathbf{1}_{r-2}\times C_4$ is the $r$-extension of the 4-cycle, that is the $r$-uniform hypergraph of four edges obtained by joining a set of $r-2$ vertices to each edge of $C_4$. $\mathrm{forb}(n,F)$ is the largest number of edges of a simple hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices without \emph{trace} (induced subhypergraph) $F$.
item.dc:creator: Richard P. Anstee, Attila Sali, Pei Wu

item.title: The combinatorial Hopf algebra of signed graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.03959v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras (CHA) is a powerful framework for studying algebraic invariants of combinatorial objects. For instance, Stanley's chromatic symmetric function and the chromatic polynomial arise naturally from the CHA of graphs. In this paper, we define a CHA of signed graphs in order to study, in the same spirit, invariants of signed graphs such as the signed chromatic polynomial. The key ingredient of our construction is a well-chosen character, from which the signed chromatic invariants are obtained. Via the antipode, we obtain new proofs of combinatorial reciprocity results for these invariants. Moreover, by deforming the character with an additional parameter, we incorporate bivariate invariants into this framework, both for classical and signed graphs. In the classical case, this technique recovers the Tutte polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Christophe Aval, Raquel Melgar

item.title: Improved Bounds for the Bilu-Linial Conjecture via Spectral Recovery from Mixed Determinantal Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.15715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bilu and Linial conjectured that every finite $d$-regular graph with $d \geq 2$ admits an edge signing $\sigma$ whose signed adjacency matrix $A_\sigma$ has spectral radius at most $2\sqrt{d-1}$. We prove that every signing meeting the mixed-root condition $r_{A_\sigma}\leq\sqrt{2(d-1)}$ satisfies \[ \rho(A_\sigma) < \frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}\sqrt{d-1}, \] where $r_{A_\sigma}$ is the largest root of the mixed determinantal polynomial $\chi[A_\sigma,-A_\sigma]$. The interlacing theorem of Ravichandran and Srivastava guarantees a signing satisfying the mixed-root condition, so our result improves the coefficient $2\sqrt2$ in their two-sided spectral bound. In the proof, we construct a positive matrix-valued probability measure supported on the roots of $\chi[A_{\sigma},-A_{\sigma}]$. The second moment gives a simple matrix inequality $A_{\sigma}^2 + dI \preceq 4r_{A_\sigma}^2I$, which yields a preliminary coefficient $\sqrt{7}$. Estimates for the fourth moment use information about short walks to obtain the coefficient $(3+\sqrt{5})/2$. For triangle-free graphs, the coefficient improves to $\sqrt6$, and for graphs with girth at least five, it improves to $\sqrt{35/6}$. As a result of independent interest, we extend the construction to $\chi[A_1,\ldots,A_k]$ for Hermitian matrices $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ with zero diagonal, and compute the first two moments explicitly. Finally, an explicit signing of $K_8$ shows that the mixed-root condition alone cannot guarantee a coefficient below $(4+\sqrt5)/\sqrt6$.
item.dc:creator: Fangfang Lin, Hong Zhou

item.title: Tur\'an problems with bounded matching number in $k$-uniform hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.24353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, $ex_k(n,\mathcal{F})$ denotes the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graph. Let $M_{s+1}^k$ denote a matching of size $s+1$ in $k$-uniform hypergraphs. Recently, Alon and Frankl (JCTB, 2024) determined $ex_2(n,\{M_{s+1}^2,K_{\ell+1}\})$ for all $n\geq 2s+1$ and $\ell\geq 2$. For every non-bipartite graph $F$, Gerbner (JGT, 2024) determined $ex_2(n,\{M_{s+1}^2,F\})$ for sufficiently large $n$. In this paper, we investigate this problem for different ranges of the matching parameter. First we prove that for every graph $F$ with $\chi(F)>3$, there exist constants $\beta>0$ and $s_0$ such that $ex_2(n,\{M^2_{s+1}, F\})=ex_2(2s+1,F)$ for $\max\{s_0,n/2-\beta n\}<s<n/2$. For integers $\ell\ge k\ge3$, let $\mathcal{K}_{\ell+1}^k$ be the family of all $k$-graphs $F$ with at most $\binom{\ell+1}{2}$ edges for which there is an $(\ell+1)$-set $L$ such that every pair of vertices of $L$ is covered by an edge of $F$, and let $H_{\ell+1}^k$ be the $k$-uniform hypergraph obtained from the complete graph $K_{\ell+1}$ by enlarging each edge with a set of $k-2$ new vertices, which is a member of $\mathcal{K}_{\ell+1}^k$. We determine $ex_k\bigl(n,\mathcal{K}_{\ell+1}^k\cup\{M_{s+1}^k\}\bigr)$ for $s< \frac{n}{8(k-1)^{k-2}(\ell-1)^3}$. For sufficiently large $s$, we also determine $ex_k\bigl(n,\{M_{s+1}^k,H_{\ell+1}^k\}\bigr)$ for $\frac{n}{k}-\beta n<s\leq \frac{n-k}{k}$ and $s< \frac{n}{8(k-1)^{k-2}(\ell-1)^3}$.
item.dc:creator: Jialin Liu, Mingyang Guo, Xiumei Wang

item.title: Asymptotic maximum spectral radius of nonregular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.04947v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\lambda_1(n,\Delta)$ be the maximum adjacency spectral radius among connected nonregular simple graphs of order $n$ and maximum degree $\Delta$. Using effective resistance bounds, explicit comparison graphs and a one-dimensional Wirtinger inequality, we prove that, for every fixed integer $\Delta\ge3$, $\lambda_1(n,\Delta)=\Delta-c_\Delta\pi^2/(4n^2)+O_\Delta(n^{-5/2})$ as $n\to\infty$, where $c_\Delta=\Delta-1$ for odd $\Delta$ and $c_\Delta=2(\Delta-2)$ for even $\Delta$. This proves the asymptotic conjecture posed by Liu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 169 (2024), Conjecture 7.1].
item.dc:creator: Hangxi Cha, Haiying Shan

item.title: Maximum 2-scattered subspaces of $V(r,q^6)$ for every $r\geq 3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.08237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that for every prime power $q$ and every integer $r\geq 3$ there exists a maximum $2$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^6)$, that is, a $2r$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace meeting every $2$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_{q^6}$-subspace in dimension at most $2$. Since an example in dimension three is known and direct sums preserve the property, it suffices to treat $r=4$ and $r=5$. For $r=4$ we study the subspaces $U_b=\{(x,x^q+bx^{q^5}):\mathrm{Tr}_{q^{12}/q^4}(x)=0\}$ of $\mathbb{F}_{q^{12}}^2$, $b\in\mathbb{F}_{q^{12}}$. We describe the parameters $b$ for which $U_b$ is not maximum $2$-scattered in terms of trace conditions and Dickson determinants, and deduce that at least $\frac{1}{2}q^{12}-q^{11}+O(q^{10})$ parameters work; this number is positive for $q\geq 3$, and a computer search settles $q=2$. For every $r\geq 5$ coprime to $6$ we show that $U_s=\{x+\varepsilon s\,x^{q^r}:x\in\mathbb{F}_{q^{2r}}\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{q^{6r}}$ is maximum $2$-scattered for all $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{F}_{q^6}\setminus\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ and $s\in\mathbb{F}_{q^r}\setminus\mathbb{F}_q$. Consequently, $\mathbb{F}_{q^6}$-linear $[2r,r,4]_{q^6/q}$ MRD codes exist for every $r\geq 3$; for $r$ coprime to $6$, the codes obtained from $U_s$ are equivalent to their duals.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bartoli, Francesco Ghiandoni, Alessandro Giannoni, Giuseppe Marino, Alessandro Neri

item.title: New graph invariants based on $p$-Laplacian eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2310.08189v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present monotonicity inequalities for certain functions involving eigenvalues of $p$-Laplacians on signed graphs with respect to $p$. Inspired by such monotonicity, we propose new spectrum-based graph invariants, called (variational) cut-off adjacency eigenvalues, that are relevant to certain eigenvector-dependent nonlinear eigenvalue problem. Using these invariants, we obtain new lower bounds for the $p$-Laplacian variational eigenvalues, essentially giving the state-of-the-art spectral asymptotics for these eigenvalues. Moreover, based on such invariants, we establish two inertia bounds regarding the cardinalities of a maximum independent set and a minimum edge cover, respectively. The first inertia bound enhances the classical Cvetkovi\'c bound, and the second one implies that the $k$-th $p$-Laplacian variational eigenvalue is of the order $2^p$ as $p$ tends to infinity whenever $k$ is larger than the cardinality of a minimum edge cover of the underlying graph. We further discover an interesting connection between graph $p$-Laplacian eigenvalues and tensor eigenvalues and discuss applications of our invariants to spectral problems of tensors.
item.dc:creator: Chuanyuan Ge, Shiping Liu, Dong Zhang

item.title: Local Geometric and Transport Properties of Networks that are Generated from Hyperuniform Point Patterns
item.description: arXiv:2511.21082v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hyperuniformity, which is a type of order that is characterized by the suppression of long-range density fluctuations in comparison to the fluctuations in standard disordered systems, has emerged as a powerful concept in many natural and engineered phenomena. In this paper, we harness hyperuniform point patterns to generate disordered, spatially-embedded networks that are distinct from both perfectly ordered lattices and uniformly random spatial networks. We refer to this class of disordered networks as \emph{hyperuniform-point-pattern-induced (HuPPI) networks}, and we compare them to counterpart \emph{Poisson-point-pattern-induced (PoPPI) networks} and networks that we generate from random-sequential-adsorption (RSA) packings (which have local order but are not hyperuniform). We examine HuPPI, PoPPI, and RSA networks that we generate using Gabriel, Delaunay, Delaunay-centroidal, and Voronoi network-generation methods. We show that HuPPI networks have smaller mean normalized total effective resistances (TERs) than PoPPI networks in Gabriel, Delaunay-centroidal, and Voronoi networks and have shorter mean random-walk mixing times than PoPPI networks in Gabriel, Delaunay, and Delaunay-centroidal networks. For all four network-generation methods and for both HuPPI and PoPPI networks, we find that the Ollivier--Ricci curvature (ORC) of an edge is negatively correlated with its TER edge contribution (i.e., the increase in TER that results from removing that edge). Collectively, our results (1) illustrate how the local network geometry that ORC measures is related to transport and network connectivity and (2) demonstrate that the network-generation method provides an additional design lever for spatial networks beyond the choice of their underlying point pattern. [This abstract is abridged significantly from the full abstract.]
item.dc:creator: James V. Raj, Xiaohan Sun, Charles Emmett Maher, Katherine A. Newhall, Mason A. Porter

item.title: Hindman and Owings-like theorems without the Axiom of Choice
item.description: arXiv:2603.27163v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate Hindman- and Owings-type Ramsey-theoretic statements in Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory without the Axiom of Choice, with some occasional extra assumptions (such as the Axiom of Dependent Choice and/or the Axiom of Determinacy). We study several variations of Hindman's theorem on $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces; notably, we show that the uncountable analog of Hindman's theorem fails for the additive group of $\mathbb R$ (under ZF), and for $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces of uncountable dimension (under DC if such dimension is not well-orderable), among other results. In contrast, for Owings-type configurations, we obtain several positive results, especially when assuming AD. These results highlight the interaction between determinacy, algebraic structure, and dimension in the study of infinite Ramsey theory without the Axiom of Choice.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e A. Guzm\'an-Vega, David J. Fern\'andez Bret\'on, Eliseo Sarmiento Rosales

item.title: Extensions of the Carlitz-McConnel and Blokhuis-Sziklai theorems for unions of cyclotomic classes
item.description: arXiv:2604.04126v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime, let $q=p^n$, and let $D\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^\ast$. A celebrated result of Carlitz and McConnel states that if $D$ is a proper subgroup of $\mathbb{F}_q^\ast$, and $f:\mathbb{F}_q\to\mathbb{F}_q$ is a function such that $(f(x)-f(y))/(x-y)\in D$ for all $x\neq y$, then $f$ must be of the form $f(x)=ax^{p^j}+b$. In this paper, we extend their result to the setting where $D$ is a union of cosets of a fixed subgroup of $\mathbb{F}_q^\ast$, under a mild assumption. In a similar spirit, we also investigate maximum cliques in related Cayley graphs over finite fields, strengthening several results of Blokhuis, Sziklai, and Asgarli and Yip.
item.dc:creator: Maosheng Xiong, Chi Hoi Yip

item.title: The Symmetric Hit Problem in Four Variables: Relative Cohits and Stabilizer-Fixed Preimages
item.description: arXiv:2606.02626v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we study the symmetric hit problem in four variables by analyzing the relative cohit space, defined as the kernel of the inclusion-induced map from symmetric to ordinary cohits. Theoretically, we establish that this relative space is isomorphic to a kernel in the first group cohomology of the permutation group and, equivalently, to an $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel for the general linear group, equipped with a canonical action of the normalizer quotient. Furthermore, bypassing conditional descent hypotheses, we utilize explicit Lucas--Cartan identities to construct unconditional fixed Steenrod preimages for nontrivial stabilizers, resolving infinite families of monomials strictly above the minimal-spike weight. Using the ordinary and symmetric Kameko isomorphisms, we reduce the determination of complete bases in two generic degree families to exact calculations in degrees one, three, six, ten, and sixteen. We discover that universal relative vanishing fails: the relative space is non-trivially one-dimensional in degree fifteen and forms an indecomposable two-dimensional normalizer module in degree eighteen. In the family $5\cdot2^t-4$, the symmetric cohit dimension stabilizes at six and the relative dimension at one for $t\geq2$; in the family $7\cdot2^t-4$, they are four and zero for $t\geq1$. We give complete bases by explicit exponent formulas and prove Janfada's monomial implication in every degree of both families. A general numerical threshold determines the finite initial degree from which Kameko isomorphisms apply, and a direct-sum formula transports the entire symmetric hit basis.
item.dc:creator: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev

item.title: Pythagorean triples in level sets of completely multiplicative functions
item.description: arXiv:2607.04903v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that given completely multiplicative functions $f_1,\dots,f_d$ taking values in the unit circle, there exist Pythagorean triples (i.e., integer solutions to $x^2+y^2=z^2$) with $f_i(x),f_i(y),f_i(z)$ all arbitrarily close to $1$ for all $i$. This is a new special case of the conjecture that any finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ has a monochromatic Pythagorean triple. Our proof combines vanishing averages for aperiodic functions with concentration estimates for pretentious functions. A similar proof is applied to obtain the analogous statement for more general equations of the form $ax^2+by^2=cz^2$ whenever $a,b,c$ are perfect squares satisfying the Rado's condition.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme Azevedo, Joel Moreira

item.title: Formalizing Flag Algebras in Lean
item.description: arXiv:2607.23500v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Razborov's flag algebra method is one of the most successful tools for proving asymptotic density inequalities in extremal graph theory. It reduces an inequality about all large graphs avoiding a forbidden pattern to finitely many algebraic conditions, and a certificate satisfying them can be found by semidefinite programming. We formalize the method for finite simple graphs in Lean 4, building on Mathlib. The formalization covers flags and their densities, the flag algebra as a quotient vector space, positive homomorphisms as limits of graph sequences, Razborov's random extensions, and the downward operator that averages out labels. On top of this theory, we build verified computation of flag densities and a tactic that turns certificates found by semidefinite programming into Lean proofs. The certificate serves only as candidate data; Lean checks every fact the proof uses. With this development we verify seven Tur\'an-type upper bounds. Adding lower-bound constructions proved in Lean yields the asymptotic form of Mantel's theorem and the asymptotic Erd\H{o}s pentagon theorem $\pi(C_5;K_3)=24/625$; to our knowledge, the latter has not previously been formalized in a proof assistant. We also prove two inequalities of Goodman. All density theorems reported here depend only on the standard axioms of Lean's logic. Formalization also led us to treat forbidden subgraphs with a different semantics. Instead of building a separate flag algebra for each forbidden family, we keep a single algebra of all graphs and impose the constraint only when interpreting an inequality, through randomly labeled limits of graphs satisfying it. We prove that this ensemble semantics yields the intended density bounds, and that a condition we call root-plantability characterizes when it agrees with the standard semantics.
item.dc:creator: Gyeongwon Jeong, Seonghun Park, Jihoon Hyun, Sang-il Oum, Hongseok Yang

item.title: Estimates for $L^p$ variants of Gowers norms
item.description: arXiv:2609.08916v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by a log-convexity question of Bennett and Tao, we consider Gowers-type functionals defined by $L^p$ norms of multiple autocorrelations. We prove sharp bounds in terms of $L^q$ norms and characterise the near-extremisers on Euclidean spaces as well as locally compact abelian groups. We also establish two families of degree-lowering inequalities and study their near-extremisers. As a byproduct of this broader theory, we show that the constant in the log-convexity estimate for Gowers norms is strictly less than unity, confirming the aforementioned conjecture of Bennett and Tao. Finally, we characterise the $p$ for which the Gowers-type functionals necessarily satisfy the triangle inequality on nonnegative measurable functions.
item.dc:creator: Vjekoslav Kova\v{c}, Keith M. Rogers

item.title: Stability of plethysm coefficients and modified polynomial induction
item.description:
arXiv:2610.07929v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $h_n$ denote the complete homogeneous symmetric function of degree $n$, $s_
u$ the Schur function indexed by a partition $
u$, and $\langle\cdot,\cdotangle$ the Hall inner product. The plethysm coefficient $\langle h_n[h_m], s_
uangle$ is the multiplicity of the Weyl module $W_
u(\mathbb{C}^N)$ in $\mathrm{Sym}^n(\mathrm{Sym}^m(\mathbb{C}^N))$ whenever $
u$ has at most $N$ parts. For a partition $\lambda$, let $\lambda[mn]=(mn-|\lambda|,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots)$. Bowman and Paget proved that $\langle h_n[h_m], s_{\lambda[mn]}angle$ is independent of $m$ and $n$ once $m,n\ge|\lambda|$. We prove that this coefficient is already constant for $m\ge\lambda_1$ and $n\ge\lfloor(|\lambda|+\lambda_1)/2floor$, and that its stable value equals $\langle s_\lambda, H[H-1-h_1]angle$, where $H=\sum_{i\ge0}h_i$; the proof uses the skewing operators adjoint to multiplication by complete homogeneous symmetric functions. We give a short new proof of the Bowman-Paget theorem based on stability of vector-partition functions, which count the ways of writing a vector of non-negative integers as an unordered sum of non-zero such vectors (its parts). Using a Vandermonde-type determinantal identity, we deduce that the stable value is a signed sum of numbers of vector partitions all of whose parts have entries summing to at least 2. The same method gives a short proof of Brion's stability theorem. We show that the stable value equals the multiplicity of $W_\lambda(\mathbb{C}^k)$, where $k=\lfloor|\lambda|/2floor$, in an explicit representation of $GL_k(\mathbb{C})$ independent of $m$ and $n$, obtained by modifying the polynomial induction of Narayanan, Paul, Prasad and Srivastava. Finally, we prove an explicit positive formula for the stable value, which counts the number of lattice points in a polytope, when $\lambda_1\le 4$.
item.dc:creator: Soumyadip Sarkar

item.title: Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers
item.description: arXiv:2610.11965v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p_i$ be the $i$th prime, and let $f(N)$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of \[ \left\{\prod_{i=1}^N p_i^{a_i}:0\le a_i<N,\ a_i\in\mathbb{Z}\right\} \] containing no two distinct legs of an integer right triangle. We prove \[ f(N) \ll N^N (\log\log N)^{-1/1296}. \]
item.dc:creator: Rongzhong Xiao

item.title: Insertion and expansion of cylinders around the unit ball
item.description: arXiv:2610.13972v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A unit ball is surrounded with a ring of $n$ equal infinite circular cylinders. Each cylinder touches the ball and its two neighbors. Can one more cylinder of the same radius be added if the configuration may be rearranged? Can the $n$ cylinders instead be enlarged, and by how much? We prove that insertion is impossible for $3\le n\le7$ and possible for $n\ge9$. The case $n=8$ remains open. The case $n=6$ is Kuperberg's problem from 1990, which was resolved recently. We prove that the ring of four cylinders cannot be expanded. This settles a conjecture of Ogievetsky and Shlosman from 2018. For $n\ge5$ the largest possible expansion radius remains unknown.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mati\'c, Rado\v{s} Radoi\v{c}i\'c, Andreas Spomer

item.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
item.description: arXiv:2610.14467v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang
